goal: Reduce repeated packet context while binding every reference to the compiled requirement identity
asset: Packet context, compiler estimates and shipped graph templates
scope: Opt-in reference projection with compact IDs
Exact compiled identity validation before packet reads
Reference context as the shipped template default
outOfScope: Dropping full-packet review when a reviewer needs it

record.question: How should nodes consult a large locked packet without repeating its whole text in every context?

options.strongest_objection: Nodes must read relevant packet sections from a verified file before use
Every lens and refuter repeats tens of thousands of scope tokens on every model call

record.rationale: Retain the full identity in summaries and a compact catalogue in prompts; a first-command identity check binds local and archived bytes to the exact compiled lock.
evidence: Issue #184 measured 70K packet tokens repeated on 48-121 model calls per review
Current identity already binds referenced archive digests

costs.cost: One local identity validation and targeted packet reads per node
evidence: Local specification validator already resolves and hashes archives

costs.cost: About 3.4M-8.5M repeated cache-read packet tokens per review in measured downstream run

requirements.statement: Reference prompts omit archive text and retain IDs, exact compiled identity and mandatory validation; both changed packets and changed archives refuse even after relock; estimates reflect the smaller input
requirements.counterexample: Relocking changed archives makes an old compiled reference graph trust new bytes or estimates still price the inline packet

checks.scope: Real locked archive packets, emitted JavaScript, CLI identity validation and shipped template choices
assumptions: Model workers follow their first-command instruction as they already follow inline packet requirements; filesystem validation is deterministic

challenges.claim: Does a valid current lock prove it is the lock this graph was compiled against?
challenges.resolution: No. The reference preamble includes the compiled identity digest; --check-identity compares the current validated identity against that exact digest.
